title: From client meeting to paid invoice: How Zoom and Bonsai can simplify your tool stack
summary: See how Zoom Workplace and Bonsai connect the client journey — from first meeting notes to proposals, deliverables, and paid invoices.
body_markdown:
You just finished a great client call. You nailed the pitch. They're interested. Now what?


You open your notes app to reconstruct what was said. Then your proposal tool to draft the scope. Then your project manager to set deadlines. Then your invoicing software to create the bill. Then your payment processor to actually get paid.


Five tools. Five logins. Five places something can slip through the cracks. And *you're* the human connector between all of them — copying, pasting, updating, chasing.


That's the real tax on a small business. Not the client work. The admin between the client work.


At[Zoomtopia 2026](https://events.zoom.us/ejl/AnecRuRoDxJbXDsaJ-KsVCMFXFlRNt5D1hqlul4LnM_Gcy4pb_bA~AyR39ssOWdCajWVe-Mus9m2sxCoswSgBS-zIE7-6Axiff8egfq-Y7VjDRQEnr4gGBD--WY0rrJjXTGMFDiPG-1huLFji-g_XlZA6T-5kKVage2QOHi2jLt-GqlnOYa-_zXW-iSh-EjjF-4ouSN2Zc3eF-xjYwBvlZ5Leev3Mm-4zuYAudATgSm5RQT-HAJvDvXb4GJDvq5F-5zA7ROoApO2nxayZ-k2KAsTPvoYYAEoLK-10vP3jEzxW2I-o19) , Zoom showed a different way. In the SMB Connect track session *"Connected tools: From meeting to payment,"* Sara Staffaroni (who runs Zoom's product marketing for SMB) and Laure Albouy (who runs product marketing at Bonsai by Zoom) walked through what happens when your meeting platform and your business operations platform actually talk to each other.


The result? A first client call flows into a drafted proposal, a polished deliverable, and a paid invoice.

## The problem: most tools weren't built to work together


During the session, Sara and Laure polled the audience: *"How many separate tools are you using to run your business right now?"*


The majority answered **six or more** .


That tracks with what Zoom hears from small business owners every day. The disconnected stack — meeting tool, notes app, project manager, proposal builder, invoicing software, CRM — creates gaps things can fall through. And the smaller your team, the more those gaps can cost you, because there might not be an operations person to catch what slips.


## Step 1: My Notes captures the conversation, so you can stay focused on it


The demo followed a fictional brand strategy consultant named Emma — inspired by real Zoom customers — through a complete client engagement.


Emma has just finished her first Zoom call with an ecommerce pet brand called Omzo Pets. During the call,[My Notes](https://www.zoom.com/en/products/ai-assistant/features/ai-note-taking/) captured key decisions and action items. Emma stayed fully present during the conversation because she knew everything important would be waiting for her in a structured summary.


If you caught[Session 1 of SMB Connect](https://events.zoom.us/ejl/AnecRuRoDxJbXDsaJ-KsVCMFXFlRNt5D1hqlul4LnM_Gcy4pb_bA~A_RNrLvKisB7h6lL-8ELmcBqc8T0w7nKB-Ah7tJZXeCuRfUkgO-8lM-mYG1oRxhYqMM-7vnfDGDpBk-hYjMi-VNSehwwAxYp-FCfh-6_x4-4SMIikttHjS-JMpVbnpUVpNXqlJT-WIw0bVDvbGN1qcpj-8h6rDdr1V4jf7wgx-B60EZC_kE5tLILDI-VEuNaTFwdUQ-nl7v-dfCyf9YBOeXlp2th--GICAqpAacf9mULG-iWABXh1906I63r-y) , you already saw Jen Chiou from Quest Craft use My Notes the same way. Session 3 takes that concept and shows what happens *after* the follow-up — when the captured context flows forward into the actual business workflow.


## Step 2: Meeting notes flow into your CRM automatically


Emma opens her client record in her[Bonsai CRM](https://www.zoom.com/en/products/bonsai/features/crm/) — Zoom's client management solution — and the meeting notes are already there. Because she'd set up the integration, they synced automatically. Along with the attendee list and the Zoom recording link.


No copy-paste. No manual entry. The context from the conversation sits alongside the rest of the client relationship: emails, calendar events, and everything else Emma needs.


This is the moment that resonated with Katie, an architect who runs her own firm:


> *"Zoom takes notes for me, and then it puts those notes into Bonsai — it does it automatically. Before, I had a file for each project on my computer. Now if a client calls me, I can pull it right up and see exactly what we talked about."*


## Step 3: AI helps draft your proposal from the conversation


Emma's next step is to send Omzo Pets a proposal. Instead of starting from a blank page, she opens[Bonsai's Proposal Builder](https://www.zoom.com/en/products/bonsai/features/proposals/) — and it drafts a proposal based on what was discussed in the meeting. *(Note: Bonsai's AI-powered Proposal Builder is coming soon.)*


She's not writing the proposal. She's directing it. Bonsai generates a structured outline — scope, deliverables, timeline — and Emma reviews, edits, and makes it her own. She adds e-signing, sets her pricing from her pre-built service library, and configures the proposal to automatically create a draft invoice once the client accepts.


Then she sends it. And she'll know the moment Omzo Pets opens it.


## Step 4: Create polished deliverables without starting from scratch


Omzo Pets signs the proposal. Now the real work begins — and this is where many consultants open a blank document and lose an afternoon.


Not Emma. She opens[Zoom Canvas](https://www.zoom.com/en/products/collaborative-docs/) and gives the AI the link to her Omzo Pets meeting notes. She prompts it to create a brand positioning brief with sections for Brand Voice, Target Audience, Competitive Landscape, and Recommended Taglines.


In moments, she has a structured brief with tables, callout boxes, and real sections she can hand to her client. Then she applies Canvas's polish feature — picking from a few presentation styles — to transform the working document into a clean, client-ready layout that looks exactly how she wants to present it to Omzo Pets.


She even takes the Competitive Landscape section and feeds it into **AI Slides** to generate two focused slides breaking down the key competitors, the positioning gaps, and where Omzo Pets fits in.


The difference between handing a client a working doc and handing them something that looks like it was designed for them.

## Step 5: Get paid without chasing the invoice


Once Emma delivers her work, it's time to get paid. She has set up a workflow in[Bonsai](https://www.zoom.com/en/products/bonsai/features/invoicing/) , and her invoice draft is already waiting — created from the accepted proposal. Services, rates, and client details all carried over automatically.


She customizes the logo and header, sets a late fee, chooses her payment method, adds a personal message, and turns on automatic payment reminders. If Omzo Pets doesn't pay by the due date, Bonsai follows up for her.


On the client's end, the invoice arrives as a clean, professional webpage — not a PDF attachment. The amount is clear. They pick a payment method and pay.


On Emma's end, the payment hits, Bonsai marks the project as paid, and that's it.


From first Zoom call to final payment.


## Why this matters for your business


Scott, who runs design agency Dezignseed Consulting, put it simply:


> *"I was using about six different tools before. Now I can do my proposals directly in here, connected to the project already, collect upfront payment. Bonsai has automated a lot of things that I had to spend multiple steps doing before, and it's saved me a ton of time."*


When your tools work together, three things can happen:


- **Less falls through the cracks.** Meeting context can flow into your CRM, your proposals, and your invoices without you re-entering anything.
- **You look like a bigger operation than you are.** Your clients can get a seamless experience from first conversation to paid invoice — and they never see the seams between your tools, because there are none.
- **You get hours back.** The admin between meetings — the copying, pasting, reformatting, and chasing — can disappear.


As Sara put it in the session's closing: *"The tools your business runs on should work as hard as you do. And they should work together — so you're not the one filling in the gaps between them."* She added: *"You've trusted Zoom for years with your most important conversations because it just works. Now, let it take some work off your plate and replace the patchwork of tools you're juggling."*
